faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Headset Crown Race suitable for 1-1/8" split crown race for fork interface?
faq.a: Titanium Headset Crown Race uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address headset hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Headset Crown Race?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Headset Crown Race is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for 118 split crown requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Headset Crown Race require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. 118 split crown components require Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for 118 split crown application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Headset Crown Race shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Headset Crown Race includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet 118 split crown specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
